# dsh-skill-gated-tools
简体中文
**Keep specialized tools out of the way. Load a skill to get its guidance and tools together.**
Skill-gated tool discovery for DeepSeek Harness. Supports third-party plugin tools and **MCP tools**
, with individual tool rules: a fresh Agent starts with assigned tools hidden, and a successful skil
l load unlocks them for immediate use in the same turn.
## Why unlock tools through skills?
Many infrequently used tools belong to specific workflows that also need instructions, constraints o
r examples. Binding those tools to a skill lets one skill load provide both the guidance and the cap
abilities needed to act on it. General conversations carry fewer specialized tool definitions; a rel
evant task brings in the corresponding skill and tools.
Tool search follows “search for a capability → discover tools → call them.” This plugin follows “loa
d a task skill → receive its guidance and assigned tools → call them.” For models already familiar w
ith skill loading, reusing that entry point may be more natural, especially when a specialized tool
already calls for supporting instructions. **This is a workflow design rationale. We have not run co
mparative accuracy, latency or cost benchmarks against tool search.**
## Install
Install into the DSH profile where you want the rules to apply. Claude skill discovery requires the
official filesystem skill provider from DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 or a compatible version.
For a published npm release in Desktop:

1. Open **Plugins** in the sidebar.
2. Click **Add plugin**.
3. Enter `dsh-skill-gated-tools`.
4. Cl
ick **Install**, then enable it as prompted.
Package-name installation requires an npm release. Before registry publication, use the absolute pat
h to the supplied local plugin archive in the same dialog.
For Web / CLI, replace `<web-profile>` with the profile used to start your Web Host. After npm publi
I, replace `<web-profile>` with the profile used to start your Web Host. After npm publication, run:

Web and Desktop can use different profiles and plugin collections. Check which Host you are configur

## Configure tool visibility
Open **Settings → Skill-gated tools**. Search or filter the tools, select one or several, choose a p
→ Skill-gated tools**. Search or filter the tools, select one or several, choose a policy, and save.
| Policy | What the current Agent sees |

| Available | The tool is visible from the start. |
| Skill-gated | The tool appears after a success

ful load of any assigned skill. |
| Always blocked | The tool stays hidden, even after a skill loads

load of any assigned skill. |
| Always blocked | The tool stays hidden, even after a skill loads. |
Each Agent unlocks independently; resumed sessions restore successful skill-load history. A tool can
be assigned to several skills, and loading any one unlocks it. Blocking takes precedence.
### Preview directly available tools
Click the **Available** filter to preview the tool list provided at the start of a fresh session.
### Select tools and bind a global skill
For example, select the MCP resource tools in the table, choose **Skill-gated**, select the global `
mcp` skill, and **Save rules**.
The annotations follow the action order. Because the editor sits above the tool table, their visual
order from top to bottom is 2, 3, 4, 1.
### MCP tools are supported
Select MCP tools individually or bind several at once, just like other plugin tools. This example bi
nds image generation, video generation and generation-result retrieval to the `ai-image-generation`
age generation, video generation and generation-result retrieval to the `ai-image-generation` skill.
### Inspect existing bindings
Click **Skill-gated** to filter the tools. The **Access rule** column shows their assigned skills.
### Always block a tool
Click **Edit** on the tool row, choose **Always blocked**, and **Save rules**.
Saving updates only selected tools and preserves unrelated rules. Failed saves retain the draft. Reo
pen a session after changing rules to apply the saved configuration.
## From hidden to immediately usable
After configuration, inspect the actual tool list in a fresh session: tools awaiting a skill and alw
ays-blocked tools are absent from the initial list.
View the initial tool-list verification screenshots
When the user asks for a meme, the Agent loads `meme`, the tool list updates, and it calls `send_mem
e` in the same turn. Newly unlocked tools do not require a new session.
## Ask an Agent to configure rules
The plugin registers the bundled **skill-gated-tools** configuration skill. For example:
> Load the skill-gated-tools skill. Bind send_meme to the meme skill and preserve all other rules.
The guide helps the Agent inspect the real catalog, update the requested rules, and read back the re
uide helps the Agent inspect the real catalog, update the requested rules, and read back the result.
**Give unlocking skills informative descriptions.** Include relevant tasks, representative tool name
s, and a clear instruction to load the skill first. The Agent can find the entry in its skill catalo
g while the tools are still hidden. For example, a description for `meme` could say:
> Find and send memes. Before using send_meme or related meme tools, load this skill to unlock them.
Update a local skill's `description`, or the registration description supplied by its plugin. This p
lugin does not automatically rewrite other skills.
## Does lazy loading affect the KV cache?
**It depends on the model protocol and the DSH adapter.** This plugin lifts tool-visibility restrict
ions; DSH determines how the definitions enter model requests.
Cache reuse relies on an unchanged prompt prefix. Routes supporting in-conversation updates can appe
nd newly available tools and context after existing history, preserving the unchanged prefix. Other
routes may rewrite leading tool definitions and lose reuse from the first changed token. New content
still needs processing, and fewer initial tool definitions do not establish a measured cost or late
cessing, and fewer initial tool definitions do not establish a measured cost or latency improvement.
